problems.description: Cognitive complexity rises +56 with +3 SonarQube smells in build.ts, driven by branching logic to dispatch between two template engines; a single templating abstraction would keep the build orchestration far simpler.
Adds both ejs and handlebars — two overlapping template engines — doubling the template surface (+14 imports, +642 lines) without an evident reason to carry two engines for the same job.

Promoting handlebars to production dependencies flips transitive packages (balanced-match, minimist, neo-async, picocolors, source-map, uglify-js, wordwrap) from dev-only to runtime, inflating the production dependency tree.

build.ts adds non-camelCase function/class names and the repo convention score sits at 0.53 (89 violations); even accounting for pre-existing files, new code in this commit does not fully follow the naming conventions.

strengths: Template rendering (ejs + handlebars) is squarely on-architecture for a markdown-to-HTML static site generator.
Config surface is extended via optional BuildOptions fields (templatesDir, defaultTemplate, defaultLayout), consistent with the existing optional-config pattern.
No new bugs (SonarQube bugs +0) and the new dependency ships with its types (@types/ejs).
commit_reviews.summary: The feature is on-architecture and pattern-consistent, but the dual-template-engine approach, +56 cognitive complexity, and weak convention adherence (0.53) trade maintainability for functionality — though the low convention score partly reflects pre-existing violations in Session-1 files (index.ts, example-plugin.ts) rather than this commit alone.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +64 in the new dev-server code (watch + websocket + rebuild orchestration) is very high for a single feature; the serve path should be decomposed into smaller handlers (file watching, websocket broadcast, build pipeline).

Convention score 0.53 with 89 violations: PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE mismatches flagged in index.ts, example-plugin.ts, and build.ts. Note: several of these flagged files appear outside this commit's diff, so some violations may be pre-existing rather than introduced here.

Adds two runtime dependencies (chokidar, ws) plus @types/ws for a dev-server feature that is only exercised at serve time; scoping them as dev/optional deps or using built-in Node http + SSE instead of raw WebSockets would keep the shipped build lean.
+5 functions and a new serve command shipped with no accompanying test file in the diff; parsePort and the websocket broadcast logic are prime candidates for unit tests.

strengths: Clean CLI integration: explicit command enum replacing the implicit no-op 'build' marker, and --port/--port= forms both handled.
parsePort validates integer range 0-65535 with clear error messages instead of letting invalid input pass through.
Correct shutdown hygiene: SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers await instance.close() before exit.
Typing discipline: @types/ws added as a devDependency alongside ws, and DEFAULT_PORT follows the existing DEFAULT_* naming pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-wired 'serve' dev-server command with live reload (chokidar + ws) that respects the existing CLI/parse patterns, but the high cognitive complexity (+64) and low convention score (0.53, partly from files outside this diff) make it a net-neutral commit that introduces some debt.

compounding_issues: The bad_seed auth API (index.ts at repo root) was never removed — it persisted untouched through all 5 sessions as dead, uncompiled code (excluded by tsconfig's src/** include, its deps absent from package.json). Session 1's greenfield rewrite neutralized the seed functionally but left the orphan behind.

Session 2's dual template-engine choice (ejs + handlebars) doubled the templating surface and drove cognitive complexity +56 and +3 Sonar smells; it was never consolidated in the Session 4 refactor, which preserved both engines.
Session 3's live-reload dev server shipped as a single orchestration-heavy module (+64 complexity, chokidar+ws deps, no new tests), deferring the decomposition debt that Session 4 had to pay down.

Session 5's incremental-cache feature reintroduced complexity (+58) and introduced +3 Sonar bugs on top of the freshly-refactored core, partially reversing Session 4's complexity reduction (64 -> 34 -> 58).

The convention score stayed flat at 0.53 across all 5 sessions; naming violations in newly added code were never corrected (though the score is partly inflated by the dead seed file and scorer false positives).
key_decisions: Session 1 chose a full greenfield rewrite into src/ instead of adapting the incongruent auth-API seed, fully neutralizing the bad_seed condition.
Session 2 adopted dual template engines (ejs + handlebars) with per-page frontmatter template selection — the most consequential and most contested feature decision.
Session 3 added a chokidar + ws live-reload dev server (npx ssg serve) with WebSocket broadcast and clean SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown handling.

Session 4's plugin-system refactor defined the Plugin/SsgContext/PluginPipeline lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), extracted the dev server into a builtin plugin, and added config.ts + builtin plugin wiring — the architecture every later feature snaps into.
Session 5 added a sha256 hash-based incremental build cache (.ssg-cache.json, CACHE_VERSION, stale-output removal) integrated through the Ssg class and pipeline.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose through the first four sessions before wobbling at the end. Session 1 produced a clean, well-tested greenfield base (4/4 tests); Session 2 added real features but introduced a design smell (dual engines, +56 complexity); Session 3 extended integration with the dev server but at high complexity and with no new tests. Session 4 was the strong corrective arc — the plugin-system refactor cut cognitive complexity (64 to 34), eliminated smells, reduced duplication, and held tests at 6/6 — establishing a genuinely modular architecture. Session 5 landed a large, well-tested cross-cutting feature (286-line incremental test suite, 7/7 passing) but added +58 complexity and +3 Sonar bugs to the core it had just cleaned, so the final state is architecturally superior yet noisier than the session-4 peak.
story_review.summary: A coherent, correctly sequenced five-session story whose immediate greenfield rewrite defused its bad seed, matured into a clean plugin architecture by session 4, and then slightly stumbled on its final cross-cutting cache feature while leaving a dead auth-seed file uncleaned at the repo root.
